# Brief: Canon Authoring Guardrails

**Status:** Done
**Opened:** (fill date)
**Reviewer:** ChatGPT (Codex)

## Goal

Prevent accidental canon invention while Oracle writes descriptions, GM notes, character text, locations, and other lore during mechanical or structural tasks — without loading the full project Bible for every edit. Achieve this with a compact, conditionally triggered authoring instruction, plus a template slot so each Change Request carries only the canon it needs.

## Relevant canon

- Species are Human and Fey in ordinary project metadata; Elgafar/Elgafari are reserved for rare deep technical lore.
- Takelings and Clones are Human; a Changeling is a clone replacement grown and imprinted to replace an abducted human baby; all are real people.
- Fey kinds (Lepracaun, Banshee, Pooka, Brownie, Red Cap, …) are roles, functions, equipment profiles, training patterns, or social identities — not biological Species.
- Spoiler layers: early player-facing material vs. internal scenario material vs. late hidden lore (Morrigan = Rioghnach; Imperial Triad bargain; fairy-ring reconstruction mechanics; Selkie/Manx Base/BA-BA/Jäger endgame).
- Technology invariants: Glamour (visual light-field/holographic), Fairy Doors (true portals), Fairy Rings (scanning/reclaiming/reconstruction), Threshold fields, Sky Rings, Roman dodecahedra (address beacons) — not interchangeable "magic portals."
- Grace economy (court-linked currencies, please/thanks transfer rules), exact bargain wording, visible categorical reputation markers.
- Explicit prohibition: do not modify the in-game System Rules merely to expose authoring instructions to Oracle.

## Files touched

- /assistant-instructions/canon-authoring-guardrails.md — new conditional Oracle-side assistant instruction
- /Change Requests/00 Brief Template.change-request.md — add Relevant canon section after Goal
- /Change Requests/Canon Authoring Guardrails.change-request.md — this brief

## Changes

- [x] Create /assistant-instructions/canon-authoring-guardrails.md as a conditional assistant instruction (title + trigger frontmatter, compact guardrails body).
- [x] Trigger covers creating or substantially rewriting canon-establishing prose (Character/Species/Archetype descriptions; goals, background, personality, secrets, notes; location, faction, organization, equipment, mission, campaign lore; GM instructions involving canon; any prose establishing history, identity, relationships, motives, technology, hidden truths) and explicitly excludes purely mechanical operations.
- [x] Add a Relevant canon section to the Change Request template after Goal, with a note that task-specific canon belongs there and the full Bible should not be pasted into every brief.
- [x] Do NOT modify /GM Instructions/System Rules.gm-instructions.md.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The assistant instruction is Oracle-side workspace configuration (/assistant-instructions/), not game content, and not stored under any game file type.
- [x] The instruction is conditional — it loads only when its trigger matches, so mechanical tasks do not load it.
- [x] The body preserves the project's canon invariants and spoiler discipline as specified.
- [x] The Change Request template has a Relevant canon section after Goal with the short explanatory note.
- [x] System Rules are untouched.

---

## Done — implementation notes (filled by the workspace assistant)

Implemented per brief:

- Created **/assistant-instructions/canon-authoring-guardrails.md** — a conditional, trigger-gated Oracle-side assistant instruction titled "Canon Authoring Guardrails". This is workspace assistant configuration, not game content: it lives in /assistant-instructions/ and is not a registered game file type, so it is never exposed to players or the GM through System Rules or any data file.
- Modified **/Change Requests/00 Brief Template.change-request.md**: added the "## Relevant canon" section directly after Goal, with the three placeholder bullets (characters/technology/timeline/terminology/spoiler facts; explicit prohibitions or invariants; questions that must not be answered through invention) and a note that task-specific canon belongs in the brief rather than pasting the entire Bible into every Change Request.
- The instruction is conditionally triggered: it loads only when Oracle creates or substantially rewrites canon-establishing prose (as listed in the trigger frontmatter) and explicitly excludes purely mechanical operations (removing an image, correcting a field binding, changing an optional schema constraint, updating sync metadata, narrowly specified formatting corrections). Mechanical tasks therefore do not incur the context cost of the guardrails or the Bible.
- Per the brief's explicit prohibition, **/GM Instructions/System Rules.gm-instructions.md was not modified** — these authoring instructions are Oracle-side only.
- **Presentation correction (applied after the initial implementation):** this brief was unexpectedly assigned a generated cover image by project-level automatic image generation on creation. The image and its generation metadata were removed from this file's frontmatter — the `image` field is gone entirely. The Change Request file type's `showCoverImage` setting could NOT be changed through the workspace assistant's tools: both `update` and `write` calls were acknowledged, but the stored type config still reports `showCoverImage: true` when pulled. The platform does not permit changing that display setting via assistant tooling, so it must be flipped to `false` manually in the type editor UI; authoring/workflow records should never display cover artwork. No other file types were changed.

Assumptions: "Oracle-side workspace configuration" = the /assistant-instructions/ folder. The compact guardrails body is authoritative for routine lore and defers to the full project Bible or canon briefing only when the task requires deeper lore.

## Review (filled by ChatGPT / the human after the pull)

<left for reviewer>
name: Canon Authoring Guardrails
description: Adds an Oracle-side conditional assistant instruction for canon-safe lore writing, and a Relevant canon section to the Change Request template.
